title: Paris, France
overview: Paris, the City of Light, is the capital of France and one of the world's greatest cities. A global centre for art, fashion, gastronomy, and culture, Paris is home to iconic landmarks like the Eiffel Tower, the Louvre, and Notre-Dame Cathedral. The city radiates romance and sophistication, offering world-class museums, Michelin-starred restaurants, charming neighbourhoods, and vibrant nightlife.
best_time_to_visit: April–June and September–October for mild weather and fewer crowds. July–August is peak tourist season and can be hot. December brings Christmas markets.
climate: Oceanic climate. Mild summers (20–25°C), cool winters (3–8°C). Rain is possible year-round; spring and autumn can be wet.

attractions.name: Eiffel Tower
attractions.description: Iconic iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars. Buy tickets online to skip queues. Summit offers panoramic views of Paris.

attractions.name: The Louvre
attractions.description: World's largest art museum housing the Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo, and 35,000+ objects. Allow at least half a day.

attractions.name: Musée d'Orsay
attractions.description: Impressionist and Post-Impressionist masterpieces including Monet, Renoir, and Van Gogh, housed in a beautiful Beaux-Arts railway station.

attractions.name: Notre-Dame Cathedral
attractions.description: Medieval Gothic cathedral on the Île de la Cité, currently under restoration after the 2019 fire. Exterior viewing is free.

attractions.name: Montmartre & Sacré-Cœur
attractions.description: Bohemian hilltop neighbourhood with the white-domed Sacré-Cœur basilica, artist squares, and sweeping city views. Free to enter the basilica.

attractions.name: Palace of Versailles
attractions.description: Opulent royal château and gardens 30 min from Paris by RER C. One of Europe's most visited attractions. Book tickets in advance.

attractions.name: Seine River Cruise
attractions.description: 1-hour boat tour past all major landmarks. Best at sunset. Multiple operators including Bateaux Mouches and Vedettes du Pont Neuf.

attractions.name: Marais District
attractions.description: Historic district with medieval streets, the Place des Vosges, Picasso Museum, and dozens of independent boutiques and galleries.

food.name: Croissants & Café
food.description: Start every morning at a local boulangerie. Maison Landemaine and Du Pain et des Idées are among the best.

food.name: Bistro Lunch
food.description: Traditional plat du jour at a neighbourhood bistro, typically includes starter, main, and carafe of wine. Avoid tourist traps on main boulevards.

food.name: Le Marché des Enfants Rouges
food.description: Paris's oldest covered market with food stalls serving Moroccan, Japanese, Italian, and French dishes. Great for a casual lunch.

food.name: Ladurée & Pierre Hermé
food.description: Famous patisseries for world-class macarons. Ladurée on Rue Royale is the original location.

food.name: Michelin-Star Dining
food.description: Paris has more Michelin-starred restaurants than any other city. Guy Savoy and Pierre Gagnaire are legendary. Book months in advance.

transport: Paris has an excellent metro (14 lines), RER trains, and buses. Buy a carnet of 10 tickets or a Navigo week pass (€30). Bike-sharing via Vélib' is great for exploring. Taxis and Uber available but expensive in traffic.

budget_guide.notes: Museum Paris Pass (2/4/6 days) covers major museums and some transport. Pre-book popular attractions to avoid queues.

tips: Learn a few French phrases – 'Bonjour', 'Merci', 's'il vous plaît' go a long way.
Validate your metro ticket before boarding to avoid fines.
Many museums are free on the first Sunday of the month.
Avoid eating on the Champs-Élysées – quality is low, prices are high.
Paris is very walkable – the best way to explore is on foot between arrondissements.
